```{r setup}
#| include: false

library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

#| include: false

df_raw <- read_csv("Data/Social_Media_Impact_on_Daily_Lives.csv")

# Rename columns to short names
df <- rename(
  df_raw,
  idx            = `...1`,
  name           = `Enter your name`,
  age            = `Enter your age (Ex: 20)`,
  gender         = `What is your gender`,
  profession     = `What is your profession?`,
  prof_hours     = `On an average how many hours a day you spend on your profession?`,
  platforms      = `What social networking sites do you use?`,
  social_hours   = `On an average how many hours a day do you spend on these sites?`,
  family_hours   = `On an average how many hours a day do you spend with your family?`,
  why_use        = `Why do you use these social networking sites?`,
  benefits       = `What are personal benefits of  using social networking sites?`,
  when_access    = `When do you access social media websites?`,
  privacy_effect = `Do you think privacy policies are effective in social networking sites?`,
  ad_influence   = `Does social media advertising influence the purchase of your product?`,
  forget_time    = `When you use social media did you forget about time?`,
  addicted       = `Do you consider yourself addicted to social media?`
)

# Fix the one row where profession = "male"
df$profession <- ifelse(df$profession == "male", NA, df$profession)

# Function to convert hour ranges to numeric midpoints
hour_midpoint <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x == "0-2"  ~ 1,
    x == "1-2"  ~ 1.5,
    x == "2-4"  ~ 3,
    x == "4-5"  ~ 4.5,
    x == "4-6"  ~ 5,
    x == "5-6"  ~ 5.5,
    x == "6-8"  ~ 7,
    x == "6+"   ~ 7,
    x == "8+"   ~ 9,
    TRUE        ~ NA_real_
  )
}

df$social_hours_n <- hour_midpoint(df$social_hours)
df$family_hours_n <- hour_midpoint(df$family_hours)

df$addicted_bin <- ifelse(
  df$addicted == "yes", 1,
  ifelse(df$addicted == "no", 0, NA)
)
```

# Initial data analysis

```{r glimpse}
dplyr::glimpse(df)
```

```{r summary-stats}
df |>
  dplyr::select(age, social_hours_n, family_hours_n) |>
  summary()
```

```{r tbl-counts}
#| tbl-cap: "Response counts for key categorical variables"

dplyr::bind_rows(
  df |>
    dplyr::count(Variable = "Gender", Value = gender) |>
    dplyr::rename(Count = n),

  df |>
    dplyr::count(Variable = "Profession", Value = profession) |>
    dplyr::rename(Count = n),

  df |>
    dplyr::count(Variable = "Addicted", Value = addicted) |>
    dplyr::rename(Count = n),

  df |>
    dplyr::count(Variable = "Forget time", Value = forget_time) |>
    dplyr::rename(Count = n)
) |>
  tidyr::drop_na(Value) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r missing-values}
df_raw |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Missing"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(Missing > 0)

df_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(`What is your profession?` == "male")
```

# Distribution plot

```{r fig-dist}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of daily social media usage and age by self-reported addiction status"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

p1 <- df |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(addicted)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    social_hours = factor(
      social_hours,
      levels = c("1-2", "3-4", "4-5", "5-6", "6+")
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::count(social_hours, addicted) |>
  dplyr::group_by(social_hours) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = social_hours, y = pct, fill = addicted)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = "fill") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("yes" = "#E07070", "no" = "#70B8E0", "not sure" = "#C0C0C0")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Addiction by Daily Screen Time",
    x = "Hours/day on social media",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Addicted?"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

p2 <- df |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = age)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "#4C9BE8", colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Age Distribution of Respondents",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

p2 + p1
```

# Data quality notes

- Time variables are categorical intervals (e.g. "3–4 hours")
- Majority of respondents are students (~78%)
- One invalid profession entry was recoded to NA
- "Not sure" responses (~24%) are excluded from binary models
